2. The short facts, giving rise to the issuance of this Rule, are that the plaintiff opposite party Nos.1-5 instituted the above suit against the petitioners and other opposite party Nos. 6-18, for permanent injunction restraining the petitioners from entering into the lands described in the schedule of the plaint. The plaintiffs'' case is that, the suit lands originally belonged to Bhawal Courts of Wards Estate as Khas Khamar and the same were recorded as such in the Khatians of the said Estate during CS Operation. The plaintiffs thereafter took settlement of the suit lands from the aforesaid Estate by two Amalnama dated 4-5-49; that on payment of a salami they were granted rent receipts and since then the plaintiffs have been possessing the land peacefully and adversely to all. It is further stated that the record was duly prepared in the name of the plaintiffs in the SA and RS Khatian on the basis of title and possession. But against the said record of right the principal defendants filed an objection under section 30 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the objection was allowed. Against the said order allowing objection the plaintiffs preferred appeal under section 31 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the appellate revenue officer set aside the order and passed an order for recording the suit land in the names of the plaintiffs. After the order of the appellate officer the plaintiffs started paying rent to the defendant No.1 Government and obtained rent receipts. It is further stated that the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land by constructing dwelling huts, cultivating the land, growing seasonal crops and planting various fruit bearing trees. The lands have been classified as Chala Bari, pond and sail, etc. The plaintiffs alleged that the defendants gave out threat to dispossess them from the suit land and hence the suit. 

 11. Mr Khondaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite parties, has filed counter affidavit to oppose the Rule. Repelling the above submissions of the learned Attorney-General it is contended by Mr Mahbubuddin Ahmed that the opposite parties had already acquired title in the suit land because of the facts that the suit land originally belonged to Bhawal Courts of Wards Estate as their Khas Khamar land and the plaintiffs along with others took settlement of the suit land from the said Estate by Amalnama on payment of salami on 4-5-49 and they were granted rent receipts by the said Estate. It has been further submitted that suit lands were subsequently recorded in the name of the plaintiffs and they (opposite party) paid rent to the government. Mr Mahbubuddin. Ahmed therefore contends that both the courts below having rightly considered the oral and documentary evidences found plaintiffs'' possession in the suit lands and prima facie title in their favour quite legally. It is therefore urged before me that in a suit for permanent injunction, the question of title is not that material to be looked into but incidentally the court can look into it.
